subject: Re: Acme RFP - Geographic SLO weighting and evidence harmonization
messages:

Subject: Acme RFP - regional weighting for Uptime/Latency SLOs

Jasmine / Lauren,

Thanks for taking our RFP. We have one open question in the SLO section around multi-region scoring: Acme runs production traffic across US-EAST and US-WEST and needs an availability SLO that reflects customer impact by geography. Please confirm the following in your response:

- Do you provide region-weighted SLO calculation by traffic share (customer-generated) or by probe/synthetic coverage?
- If you support both, how do you reconcile differences (e.g., synthetic probes show 99.95% in US-WEST but customer traffic indicates 99.7%)?
- What is the measurement window for triggering service credits (rolling 30d? calendar month?), and how is partial-region degradation attributed?

We also need example math for a multi-region incident that affects only one region for a 6-hour window.

Can you point us to an evidence package (sample telemetry exports) we can review during procurement?

Best,
Tom

Subject: Re: Acme RFP - regional weighting for Uptime/Latency SLOs

Tom — thanks for the clear questions. Attaching a short matrix (redwood-slo-weighting-matrix-v1.xlsx) and a one-page summary. High level answers here; we'll follow up with worked math and a sample telemetry bundle.

- We support both traffic-weighted and probe-weighted calculations. By default in multi-region deployments we use customer-traffic weighting when customers route production traffic across regions (this most closely matches customer impact).
- When probe and real-traffic diverge we apply a reconciliation policy:
  * Primary signal: customer request success-rate and latency percentiles (p95/p99) from production telemetry.
  * Fallback signal: synthetic probes if production telemetry is insufficient (low volume) or when probes detect systemic regional routing issues.
  * If both exist, we surface both metrics and compute a blended regional score (traffic-weighted by default). You can opt to enforce probe-only measurement in the contract.
- Measurement window: rolling 30-day window is our standard for SLO violation calculation; calendar-month billing windows are supported for crediting. Partial-region degradation is attributed to the impacted region(s) proportionally by regional traffic share during the incident window.

I'll loop Karthik for the formal formula and a worked example. I'll upload a sample evidence export to Drive by EOD.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@acme.com>, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme RFP - regional weighting for Uptime/Latency SLOs

Tom / Jasmine — adding the technical formula and a note on probes vs production measurement. See inline.

On reconciliation and calculation:

1) Regional availability score (R_i) = 1 - (failed_requests_i / total_requests_i) over the measurement window (we support p95/p99 latency similarly).
2) Global availability (A) = sum over i (w_i * R_i) where w_i is the traffic weight for region i (w_i = regional_requests_i / total_requests_global) when using traffic-weighted mode.
3) If using probe-weighted mode, w_i will be the probe-coverage weight (configured per contract).

Example for a 6-hour single-region incident (worked example below):
- US-WEST traffic share during incident: 20% (w_west = 0.2)
- US-EAST availability during incident: 100%
- US-WEST availability during incident: 96% (4% failed during 6 hours)
- Incident window relative to 30-day: 6 hours / 720 hours = 0.00833 share of window.

Blended impact on 30-day A (approx):
- Degradation contribution = w_west * (1 - R_west) * (incident_window_fraction) = 0.2 * 0.04 * 0.00833 = 0.0000667 (~0.00667% absolute impact on 30-day availability).

Service credit triggers follow your SLO thresholds — e.g., if monthly availability drops below 99.95% we compute credit by the contract formula using the calendar month or converted rolling-window equivalent per the SLA. We provide raw request logs and aggregated CSVs for the month and incident windows as evidence.

Notes on telemetry:
- We export request-level samples (time, region, request_id, status_code, latency_ms) and synthetic probe results (probe_id, region, success, rtt_ms, timestamp).
- Retention: standard is 90 days for request-level samples; aggregated SLO buckets retained 365 days. Longer retention can be contracted.

If you want, we can produce the numeric worked example in the spreadsheet for the exact dates in your RFP and a tarred evidence sample.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Tom — attaching the worked example and a sample evidence export. Summary answers below and links to the artifacts:

- Worked math: see tab "WorkedExample" in redwood-slo-weighting-matrix-v1.xlsx. We included cell-by-cell formulas and a second tab with the same calculation expressed using calendar-month normalization. Baseline (pre-incident) = 99.98% used per request. The sheet shows the delta to calendar-month availability and the credit calculation using the contract credit table.
- Export format: tar.gz containing CSVs. Files included: requests_20261001-20261031.csv, probes_20261001-20261031.csv, sampling_map.csv (boolean sampled flag), request_path_map.csv (anonymized tokens). The evidence tarball is evidence-export-sample-20261012.tar.gz.
- Sampling and anonymization: request-level CSV includes a "sampled" boolean per row. We anonymize request paths by tokenizing and hashing path segments; an additional map file maps hashed tokens to normalized labels (e.g., /v1/infer -> /v1/INFER) — no PII.

Drive link with the files: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD-example-drive-link
HubSpot reference: HS-12345

Next steps: if this looks good we can provide a longer retention quote and a signed evidence NDA to deliver full production extracts. Aditya will follow up on contract language options for calendar-month vs rolling-window crediting.

Thanks,
Jasmine
